items.title: SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via Adversarial Perturbations
items.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems improve Large Language Model (LLM) responses by incorporating information from external knowledge bases. However, recent studies have shown that attackers can extract substantial portions of private knowledge bases from RAG systems through repeated querying. Yet, state-of-the-art extraction attacks either rely heavily on external LLMs to generate adversarial queries or require a large number of queries. In this paper, we propose SNAPRAG, a novel and cost-efficient attack for extracting RAG knowledge bases through adversarial perturbations. Our approach algorithmically generates adversarial queries without relying on external LLMs and allows for a strictly configurable query budget. In particular, SNAPRAG uses a discrete token-mutation algorithm to generate novel queries in a strict black-box setting. Our adaptive dissimilarity threshold calibration systematically forces queries into unexplored semantic regions of the target database, enabling extraction with fewer queries. Specifically, to extract half of the target knowledge base, our method requires up to 6.77$\times$ fewer queries than existing approaches. Furthermore, within a fixed query budget, our method recovers up to 96.9%, outperforming the closest approach by 7.7-19.9%. We further evaluate SNAPRAG against active defenses, where it remains the leading attack on four of five defended targets, achieving 50.7-96.3% extraction rate.

items.title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
items.summary: Unplanned 30-day intensive care unit (ICU) readmission is a critical benchmark for evaluating healthcare quality. Most predictive models assume readmission risk depends solely on a patient's individual pathophysiological state, ignoring hospital operational context and resource capacity. In practice, discharge decisions are dynamic trade-offs between patient stability and bed turnover pressures. To address this gap, we develop an Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for ICU discharge risk assessment. The system combines multi-agent collaborative extraction with self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to eliminate template noise from progress notes, while constructing departmental workload indicators alongside admission flow features, continuous vital signs, and sparse medical codes (ICD/DRG). Addressing severe class imbalance (about 10.5% readmissions) and alarm fatigue, we implement data normalization, class reweighting, and decision-threshold calibration. In 20 independent runs across 20,000 ICU stays from MIMIC-III, empirical findings demonstrate that: vital signs alone have limited predictive capacity under real-world class imbalance (PR-AUC of 0.1387 +/- 0.0086); directly concatenating raw text embeddings degrades decision tree performance (XGBoost and LightGBM PR-AUC drop to 0.3893 and 0.4030); whereas an end-to-end multimodal fine-tuning architecture (Transformer E2E FineTune) utilizing layer-wise parameter freezing and differential learning rates reverses text negative transfer, achieving the highest AUROC of 0.8288 +/- 0.0110, PR-AUC of 0.4373 +/- 0.0310, and F1-Score of 0.4757 +/- 0.0196. Operational indicators supply independent risk signals, laying an engineering foundation for high-utility clinical decision support tools.

items.title: ARMOR: Adaptive Curriculum Meta-Learning for Noise-Robust RAG Reasoning
items.summary: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in mitigating hallucinations by incorporating external knowledge. However, the retrieval process inevitably introduces noise, posing significant challenges to RAG robustness. Fundamentally, noise robustness is a composite competency encompassing noise identification, retrieval filtering, and robust reasoning. Unfortunately, existing methods often fail to capture this holistic nature, typically restricted to single-dimensional enhancements or hampered by noise-induced optimization interference. To address these limitations, we decompose RAG robustness into three sub-tasks: knowledge boundary perception, retrieval verification, and robust reasoning. Accordingly, we propose ARMOR, an Adaptive Curriculum Meta-Learning for Noise Robust RAG Reasoning. Inspired by the teaching process, ARMOR introduces an adaptive task scheduler as a teacher to curate training plans according to the absolute learning progress of RAG generators (Student). Distinct from GRPO, ARMOR utilizes inter-group advantage estimation during learning to effectively mitigate mode collapse caused by limited output spaces. Experiments on three complex reasoning datasets (2WikiMultiHopQA, MusiQue, and HotPotQA) indicate that ARMOR achieves synergistic improvements in retrieval noise robustness, significantly outperforming baselines in output quality.

Dưới đây là tóm tắt nội dung 2 trang đầu tiên của bài báo **"SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via Adversarial Perturbations"** (arXiv:2611.12241v1):

---

### 1. Thông tin bài báo
* **Tiêu đề:** SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via Adversarial Perturbations
* **Tác giả:** Melih Coşğun, Mehmet Emre Gürsoy, Alptekin Küpçü, Sinem Sav (Bilkent University & Koç University, Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ)
* **Lĩnh vực:** An toàn thông tin / Khoa học máy tính (cs.CR)

---

### 2. Bối cảnh & Đặt vấn đề
* **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation):** Giúp LLM truy cập cơ sở tri thức (Knowledge Base - KB) bên ngoài để trả lời chính xác hơn. Tuy nhiên, việc đưa tài liệu nội bộ/riêng tư vào ngữ cảnh khi suy luận mở ra nguy cơ rò rỉ dữ liệu qua các cuộc tấn công **trích xuất tri thức (knowledge extraction attack)**.
* **Hạn chế của các phương pháp hiện tại (như PirateRAG, RAGThief):**
  1. Yêu cầu số lượng truy vấn lớn và không cố định, tốn kém chi phí (đặc biệt với các dịch vụ tính phí theo API như OpenAI Assistants API).
  2. Phụ thuộc lớn vào một LLM bên ngoài để tạo truy vấn tấn công, tốn tài nguyên và bị giới hạn bởi chất lượng của mô hình đó.

---

### 3. Phương pháp SNAPRAG
SNAPRAG đề xuất một giải pháp **hoàn toàn loại bỏ LLM bên ngoài**, sử dụng thuật toán đột biến token (discrete token-mutation algorithm) tên là **Qgen**:
1. **Đột biến token theo chuỗi (Qgen):** Thay đổi (perturb) các token của các đoạn văn bản đã trích xuất được để đẩy vector nhúng (embedding) của truy vấn mới ra xa các vùng đã biết, hướng tới các vùng tri thức chưa khai phá.
2. **Hiệu chỉnh ngưỡng bất đồng thích ứng (Adaptive Dissimilarity Threshold Calibration):** Tự động đo đạc khoảng cách không gian nhúng tối đa có thể đạt tới trong ngân sách generation để tạo ra $n$ mức truy vấn tấn công trải đều.
3. **Bộ lọc khử trùng lặp 3 lớp (3-level deduplication filter):** Đảm bảo các truy vấn tiếp theo không bị lặp lại không gian đã tìm kiếm, giúp khai thác tối đa nội dung KB mới.

---

### 4. Kết quả chính
* **Tiết kiệm truy vấn:** Để trích xuất được **50%** cơ sở tri thức mục tiêu, SNAPRAG cần ít hơn tới **6.77 lần** số lượng truy vấn so với các phương pháp tiên tiến nhất hiện nay.
* **Tỷ lệ phục hồi dữ liệu:** Trong cùng một ngân sách truy vấn cố định, phương pháp khôi phục tới **96.9%** dữ liệu (vượt trội hơn 7.7–19.9% so với phương pháp tốt nhất trước đó).
* **Vượt qua cơ chế phòng thủ:** Khi đối đầu với các hệ thống RAG có cài đặt phòng thủ chủ động, SNAPRAG vẫn đạt tỷ lệ trích xuất thành công từ **50.7% – 96.3%** trên 4/5 mục tiêu thử nghiệm.

Abstract
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems improve
Large Language Model (LLM) responses by incorporating
information from external knowledge bases. However, recent
studies have shown that attackers can extract substantial por-
tions of private knowledge bases from RAG systems through
repeated querying. Yet, state-of-the-art extraction attacks ei-
ther rely heavily on external LLMs to generate adversarial
queries or require a large number of queries. In this paper,
we proposeSNAPRAG, a novel and cost-efficient attack for
extracting RAG knowledge bases through adversarial pertur-
bations. Our approach algorithmically generates adversarial
queries without relying on external LLMs and allows for a
strictly configurable query budget. In particular,SNAPRAG
uses a discrete token-mutation algorithm to generate novel
queries in a strict black-box setting. Our adaptive dissimilar-
ity threshold calibration systematically forces queries into
unexplored semantic regions of the target database, enabling
extraction with fewer queries. Specifically, to extract half of
the target knowledge base, our method requires up to 6.77×
fewer queries than existing approaches. Furthermore, within
a fixed query budget, our method recovers up to 96.9%, out-
performing the closest approach by 7.7–19.9%. We further
evaluateSNAPRAG against active defenses, where it remains
the leading attack on four of five defended targets, achieving
50.7–96.3% extraction rate.
1 Introduction
Large Language Models (LLMs) have become key building
blocks in numerous applications, from chatbots to decision-
support tools [2, 25]. However, as their use has grown, so
have concerns about their security. Prompt injection attacks,
for example, demonstrate that strategically crafted inputs can
override an LLM’s original instructions, causing it to follow
commands of an attacker instead [9, 21, 22, 26, 37]. Similarly,
prompt extraction attacks have shown that specific queries
can trick models into revealing their hidden system prompts,
exposing proprietary instructions and internal settings [3, 12,
26, 29, 39]. These weaknesses highlight a core problem: the
same ability to follow instructions that makes LLMs effective
also makes them susceptible to manipulation.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) [18] systems ex-
tend LLMs by connecting them to an external, often private,
knowledge base (KB) [7, 10, 14]. In a standard RAG pipeline,
a user query is first used to find relevant documents from the
KB, and these documents are then fed into the LLM’s context
to help it generate a more accurate response. While this setup
allows access to up-to-date and domain-specific information,
it also opens up a new risk: the retrieved documents them-
selves can be leaked [19, 27, 38]. Since the LLM processes
private content during inference time, an attacker who can
manipulate the model’s output (for instance, through prompt
injection) may potentially induce the model to leak retrieved
passages verbatim.
This leads to what is known as theknowledge extraction at-
tack, where an attacker systematically queries a RAG system
with adversarial inputs to incrementally leak and reconstruct
its private KB. While several existing attacks achieve this step-
by-step extraction by appending injection commands to their
queries, the real difference between them is how they gener-
ate new queries to maximize their exploration of the KB. For
example, Maio et al. introduce PirateRAG [23], which uses
an attacker-side open-source LLM together with an anchor-
based mechanism to generate queries that actively explore the
target’s KB. Similarly, RAGThief [15] works as a black-box
attack, using an external LLM to generate continuations of
already extracted chunks to generate new queries.
While these methods are effective, they come with several
limitations. First, they require a large and often unpredictable
number of queries to the target system. This makes the at-
tack expensive when the target is a commercial RAG service
billed by usage, such as applications built on the OpenAI
Assistants API.1 The number of queries is a direct measure
of the cost because the target LLM returns chunks from its

---

### 2. Bối cảnh & Đặt vấn đề
* **RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation):** Giúp LLM truy cập cơ sở tri thức (Knowledge Base - KB) bên ngoài để trả lời chính xác hơn. Tuy nhiên, việc đưa tài liệu nội bộ/riêng tư vào ngữ cảnh khi suy luận mở ra nguy cơ rò rỉ dữ liệu qua các cuộc tấn công **trích xuất tri thức (knowledge extraction attack)**.
* **Hạn chế của các phương pháp hiện tại (như PirateRAG, RAGThief):**
  1. Yêu cầu số lượng truy vấn lớn và không cố định, tốn kém chi phí (đặc biệt với các dịch vụ tính phí theo API như OpenAI Assistants API).
  2. Phụ thuộc lớn vào một LLM bên ngoài để tạo truy vấn tấn công, tốn tài nguyên và bị giới hạn bởi chất lượng của mô hình đó.

---

### 3. Phương pháp SNAPRAG
SNAPRAG đề xuất một giải pháp **hoàn toàn loại bỏ LLM bên ngoài**, sử dụng thuật toán đột biến token (discrete token-mutation algorithm) tên là **Qgen**:
1. **Đột biến token theo chuỗi (Qgen):** Thay đổi (perturb) các token của các đoạn văn bản đã trích xuất được để đẩy vector nhúng (embedding) của truy vấn mới ra xa các vùng đã biết, hướng tới các vùng tri thức chưa khai phá.
2. **Hiệu chỉnh ngưỡng bất đồng thích ứng (Adaptive Dissimilarity Threshold Calibration):** Tự động đo đạc khoảng cách không gian nhúng tối đa có thể đạt tới trong ngân sách generation để tạo ra $n$ mức truy vấn tấn công trải đều.
3. **Bộ lọc khử trùng lặp 3 lớp (3-level deduplication filter):** Đảm bảo các truy vấn tiếp theo không bị lặp lại không gian đã tìm kiếm, giúp khai thác tối đa nội dung KB mới.

---

### 4. Kết quả chính
* **Tiết kiệm truy vấn:** Để trích xuất được **50%** cơ sở tri thức mục tiêu, SNAPRAG cần ít hơn tới **6.77 lần** số lượng truy vấn so với các phương pháp tiên tiến nhất hiện nay.
* **Tỷ lệ phục hồi dữ liệu:** Trong cùng một ngân sách truy vấn cố định, phương pháp khôi phục tới **96.9%** dữ liệu (vượt trội hơn 7.7–19.9% so với phương pháp tốt nhất trước đó).
* **Vượt qua cơ chế phòng thủ:** Khi đối đầu với các hệ thống RAG có cài đặt phòng thủ chủ động, SNAPRAG vẫn đạt tỷ lệ trích xuất thành công từ **50.7% – 96.3%** trên 4/5 mục tiêu thử nghiệm.

items.summary:
SNAPRAG: Cost-Efficient Knowledge Extraction Attack on RAG Systems via
Adversarial Perturbations
Melih Co¸ s˘gun
Department of Computer Engineering
Bilkent University, Türkiye
Mehmet Emre Gürsoy
Department of Computer Engineering
Koç University, Türkiye
Alptekin Küpçü
Department of Computer Engineering
Koç University, Türkiye
Sinem Sav
Department of Computer Engineering
Bilkent University, Türkiye
Abstract
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems improve
Large Language Model (LLM) responses by incorporating
information from external knowledge bases. However, recent
studies have shown that attackers can extract substantial por-
tions of private knowledge bases from RAG systems through
repeated querying. Yet, state-of-the-art extraction attacks ei-
ther rely heavily on external LLMs to generate adversarial
queries or require a large number of queries. In this paper,
we proposeSNAPRAG, a novel and cost-efficient attack for
extracting RAG knowledge bases through adversarial pertur-
bations. Our approach algorithmically generates adversarial
queries without relying on external LLMs and allows for a
strictly configurable query budget. In particular,SNAPRAG
uses a discrete token-mutation algorithm to generate novel
queries in a strict black-box setting. Our adaptive dissimilar-
ity threshold calibration systematically forces queries into
unexplored semantic regions of the target database, enabling
extraction with fewer queries. Specifically, to extract half of
the target knowledge base, our method requires up to 6.77×
fewer queries than existing approaches. Furthermore, within
a fixed query budget, our method recovers up to 96.9%, out-
performing the closest approach by 7.7–19.9%. We further
evaluateSNAPRAG against active defenses, where it remains
the leading attack on four of five defended targets, achieving
50.7–96.3% extraction rate.
1 Introduction
Large Language Models (LLMs) have become key building
blocks in numerous applications, from chatbots to decision-
support tools [2, 25]. However, as their use has grown, so
have concerns about their security. Prompt injection attacks,
for example, demonstrate that strategically crafted inputs can
override an LLM’s original instructions, causing it to follow
commands of an attacker instead [9, 21, 22, 26, 37]. Similarly,
prompt extraction attacks have shown that specific queries
can trick models into revealing their hidden system prompts,
exposing proprietary instructions and internal settings [3, 12,
26, 29, 39]. These weaknesses highlight a core problem: the
same ability to follow instructions that makes LLMs effective
also makes them susceptible to manipulation.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) [18] systems ex-
tend LLMs by connecting them to an external, often private,
knowledge base (KB) [7, 10, 14]. In a standard RAG pipeline,
a user query is first used to find relevant documents from the
KB, and these documents are then fed into the LLM’s context
to help it generate a more accurate response. While this setup
allows access to up-to-date and domain-specific information,
it also opens up a new risk: the retrieved documents them-
selves can be leaked [19, 27, 38]. Since the LLM processes
private content during inference time, an attacker who can
manipulate the model’s output (for instance, through prompt
injection) may potentially induce the model to leak retrieved
passages verbatim.
This leads to what is known as theknowledge extraction at-
tack, where an attacker systematically queries a RAG system
with adversarial inputs to incrementally leak and reconstruct
its private KB. While several existing attacks achieve this step-
by-step extraction by appending injection commands to their
queries, the real difference between them is how they gener-
ate new queries to maximize their exploration of the KB. For
example, Maio et al. introduce PirateRAG [23], which uses
an attacker-side open-source LLM together with an anchor-
based mechanism to generate queries that actively explore the
target’s KB. Similarly, RAGThief [15] works as a black-box
attack, using an external LLM to generate continuations of
already extracted chunks to generate new queries.
While these methods are effective, they come with several
limitations. First, they require a large and often unpredictable
number of queries to the target system. This makes the at-
tack expensive when the target is a commercial RAG service
billed by usage, such as applications built on the OpenAI
Assistants API.1 The number of queries is a direct measure
of the cost because the target LLM returns chunks from its

Figure 1: Overview of our attack. The attacker iteratively queries the target RAG system. Extracted chunks pass through a
three-level deduplication filter before being stored in the Stolen KB. New chunks are pushed to a frontier queue, where the
query generation algorithm (Qgen) generates novel query candidates by modifying extracted chunks at different levels. A ranked
dispatch strategy prioritizes the most exploratory queries. No external LLM is used at any stage.
knowledge base as part of its output, so the output token usage
is roughly equal to the number of retrieved chunks times the
chunk length. Since API providers typically charge more for
output tokens, each query should be carefully designed to ex-
tract new, non-repeating content. Second, these methods rely
heavily on an external LLM to generate attack queries, which
requires more resources and makes the attack dependent on
the quality of the local model’s output.
To address the resource-intensive nature and unpredictable
query budgets associated with LLM-based attacks, we pro-
poseSNAPRAG, a cost-efficient, algorithmic knowledge ex-
traction attack thatcompletely removes the need for an ex-
ternal LLM. Our primary objective is to replace resource-
intensive, generative query formulation with a tightly con-
trolled strategy based on discrete token mutations. Specifi-
cally, we adapt a black-box, discrete token mutation algorithm
for query generation, which we name as Qgen. This algo-
rithm perturbs the tokens of already-extracted text chunks,
methodically pushing the embedding of each new query away
from known data while maintaining domain relevance through
small, controlled modifications. By eliminating the external
LLM dependency, our approach yields twofold savings: it
incurs zero API or external resource overhead for formulating
queries, and it successfully extracts a larger volume of the
target’s retrieval database using significantly fewer API calls
to the target compared to prior work. Figure 1 illustrates the
high-level overview of our attack pipeline.
Operating without an external LLM introduces a core tech-
nical challenge for query generation: algorithmically deter-
mining how semantically novel a newly generated query must
be to discover unseen documents. We solve this challenge by
introducing a per-chunk adaptive threshold calibration mech-
anism. Before generating queries from a newly extracted
chunk, we run an unconstrained probe usingQgen to discover
the most semantically distant text reachable within the at-
tacker’s generation budget. This probe establishes a lower
bound on achievable dissimilarity, relying entirely on the at-
tacker’s resources rather than any prior knowledge of the
target system. We then establishn evenly spaced dissimilarity
targets across this reachable range, generating one specifically
mutated query for each target level. Finally, to ensure contin-
uous exploration and prevent query clustering, we employ a
chaining strategy. As each generated query is accepted, its
embedding is immediately added to the seen-embedding set
(Eseen). This chaining forces each subsequent query to push
away from all previously generated variants, systematically
spreading the adversarial queries across the target’s embed-
ding space.
